title: White Sox slugger Munetaka Murakami set to return ahead of busy weekend
content:
The Chicago White Sox survived six weeks without star slugger Munetaka Murakami, but now he is returning at a most opportune time.

The White Sox activated Murakami off the 10-day injured list Friday morning after his 35-game absence because of a strained right hamstring.

The Sox went 17-18 without Murakami, who was among the American League leaders in home runs, RBIs, slugging percentage, walks and runs when he went on the IL on May 30.

During his absence, the Sox gained ground on Cleveland in the AL Central, going from three games back to a tie atop the division. But after splitting a four-game series with the Guardians in Cleveland, the White Sox were swept at home by the Boston Red Sox this week. Chicago scored only two runs and failed to pick up an extra-base hit in three games. So they could probably use one of their best power hitters this weekend.

Murakami’s return highlights a packed weekend on the South Side. To close out the first half, the Sox host the Athletics for a three-game series, which features Friday’s sold-out game for Mexican Heritage Night and a Saturday afternoon game preceded by the team picking No. 1 in the MLB Draft. That will be followed by an alumni home run derby headlined by José Canseco.

The White Sox surprisingly signed Murakami, 26, to a two-year, $34 million deal just before his posting window closed in late December. The market cooled on him after early hype, and the Japanese home run champ proved his doubters wrong as he hit 20 homers and posted a .938 OPS in 57 games before his injury knocked him out for six weeks.

He quickly became a sensation on the South Side, selling rackloads of jerseys and bringing in fans. That was expected. But that he was contributing to a team with playoff hopes was a major surprise.

With and without Murakami, the White Sox have been one of the best stories in baseball. Two years ago, they set the modern baseball record with 121 losses, and last season they lost 102 games. After a 6-13 start, the Sox took off, and they haven’t had a full losing month yet. Thanks to their improved play, along with early appearances by the Chicago Cubs and the Los Angeles Dodgers, the team is averaging 22,736 fans per game, a modest number, but also a 39 percent increase compared with this point last season.

While Murakami’s return is key to the team’s present, their future is the focus Saturday. The Sox are drafting No. 1 for the first time since selecting Harold Baines in 1977. The Athletic’s Keith Law’s latest mock draft has them picking high school shortstop Grady Emerson over UCLA shortstop Roch Cholowsky or Georgia Tech catcher Vahn Lackey.

“It’s still a bit of an open book, but I think we all know who the candidates are here and we’re working extremely hard,” White Sox scouting director Mike Shirley said Wednesday. “You know, the Cholowsky-Emerson conversation, the Vahn Lackey conversation, these are real. They are happening. They’re happening up to the minute.”
